answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with collateralized unique identity. Each participant locks a bond in escrow to mint one voting credential, so faking a thousand agents needs a thousand bonds. Votes use quadratic weighting: influence grows with the square root of stake, so splitting capital across fake names gains nothing. A validator that catches double-signing slashes the bond, so fraud costs more than any reward. Picture a market where a nectar refinery, a lagoon trust, and a marble quarry each post one credential; an impostor cloning all three forfeits its escrow.
